card: Re-split replaces the live rig blind: stage a candidate, judge extremes, promote
deviations_from_card: Case 2 as revised: the jaw's polygon is pushed 4 px right; report.json ranks jaw first (p99 189) and every other non-static element stays below 8 (head 6.0). Per-element error is measured on the pixels an element OWNS, not inside its bbox (head's bbox contains the jaw and would share its error): a pixel belongs to the frontmost solid drawn there, or to the element whose fill invented what that solid shows; rows partition the frame (owned_px sums to W*H). Coupled file outside write_set: tools/rig/shadowrunr_rig/rigdir.py gains publish_files(out, files, depth=) (publish refactored onto a shared _publish) so promote and revert move rig bytes through rigdir byte for byte, with layers.json last; no second writer. One feat commit, not two (tests for promote need __main__ and review together). Added a 7th case pinning that promotion never loses the previous rig (second promote with nothing staged and a revert over a changed live rig both refuse, rig.prev untouched). Every run (not only --candidate) writes report.json and extremes.png beside its rig so promote has a live baseline.
notes: Finding: the rest-frame error is blind to most misplacements. In a sweep shifting each element 4 px in 4 directions on the drawn bust, only jaw (x and +y), head (x), shard (+y) and torso (-y) produced rest error; misplaced lights recompose the portrait exactly. README says so and points at extremes.png. Revert restores a half depth pair (only one of depth.png/depth.json) not at all - rigdir never keeps one without the other. Runner-up (--only <element>) not built. Synthetic images only; data/ untouched.
